title: The Supreme Court Case That Could Doom U.S. Climate Goals

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》每日简报 DealBook 的商业与政策记者。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市 DealBook 峰会的现场，采访商界、政界和文化界最具影响力的一些领袖，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼等许多嘉宾。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 您可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经过滤的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch, free, at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在 nytimes.com 上直播部分精选访谈，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果您还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得一个月的免费访问权限，畅享我们所有的深度报道。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望您能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 您一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Sabrina Tavernisi.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的萨布丽娜·塔韦尔尼西。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》栏目。

sentences.en: As the Supreme Court term comes to a close,
sentences.zh: 随着最高法院开庭期接近尾声，

sentences.en: It's expected to rule on two landmark cases involving abortion and guns.
sentences.zh: 预计它将对涉及堕胎和枪支的两起具有里程碑意义的案件做出裁决。

sentences.en: But it will also decide another major case, one that is getting far less attention.
sentences.zh: 但它还将对另一个重大案件做出裁决，而这个案件受到的关注要少得多。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Coral Davenport on a case involving climate change that could take away much of the federal government's power to regulate.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事科拉·达文波特将为我们讲述一个涉及气候变化的案件，该案件可能会剥夺联邦政府大部分的监管权力。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, June 23rd.
sentences.zh: 今天是6月23日，星期四。

sentences.en: So, Coral, tell me about the Supreme Court case you've been following.
sentences.zh: 科拉，跟我们聊聊你一直在关注的最高法院案件吧。

sentences.en: So, this case is called West Virginia v.
sentences.zh: 好的，这个案件被称为西弗吉尼亚州诉

sentences.en: EPA.
sentences.zh: 环保局案。

sentences.en: It is certainly the largest and most important climate change case to come before the Supreme Court in over a decade.
sentences.zh: 这无疑是十多年来提交给最高法院的最大、最重要的气候变化案件。

sentences.en: Fundamentally, the case is about a group of Republican attorneys general, mostly from fossil fuel-producing states,
sentences.zh: 从根本上说，这个案子涉及一群主要来自化石燃料生产州的共和党总检察长，

sentences.en: West Virginia, Kentucky, Texas, who are suing the federal government over its authority to regulate greenhouse gases from power plants.
sentences.zh: 包括西弗吉尼亚州、肯塔基州和得克萨斯州，他们就联邦政府监管发电厂温室气体的权力起诉了联邦政府。

sentences.en: And even though it's in front of the Supreme Court now, it actually goes back to the Obama administration, back to 2014.
sentences.zh: 尽管这个案子现在闹到了最高法院，但它实际上可以追溯到奥巴马政府时期，也就是2014年。

sentences.en: You know, Obama was the first president who said, I am going to prioritize dealing with climate change.
sentences.zh: 你知道，奥巴马是第一位表示“我将把应对气候变化放在首位”的总统。

sentences.en: He tried to pass a major climate change law through the Congress.
sentences.zh: 他曾试图通过国会通过一项重大的气候变化法律。

sentences.en: Of course, that famously failed.
sentences.zh: 当然，众所周知，那次尝试失败了。

sentences.en: And after that happened, and after Democrats lost control of the Congress...
sentences.zh: 在那之后，以及民主党失去对国会的控制之后……

sentences.en: I'm going to be working with Congress where I can to accomplish this.
sentences.zh: 我将尽可能与国会合作来完成这一目标。

sentences.en: Obama said...
sentences.zh: 奥巴马说……

sentences.en: But I'm also going to act on my own if Congress is deadlocked.
sentences.zh: 但如果国会陷入僵局，我也将采取自主行动。

sentences.en: I've got a phone and a pen, and I'm going to start doing these things myself.
sentences.zh: 我有一部电话和一支笔，我要开始自己着手做这些事情了。

sentences.en: I've got a pen to take executive actions, where Congress won't.
sentences.zh: 我有一支笔，可以在国会不作为时采取行政行动。

sentences.en: And I've got a telephone to rally folks around the country on this mission.
sentences.zh: 我还有一部电话，可以就这一使命号召全国各地的人们。

sentences.en: He was referring to executive action and executive authority on many fronts, but climate change was really the biggest way in which we saw Obama try to assert that power of pen.
sentences.zh: 他指的是在多条战线上的行政行动和行政权力，而气候变化确实是我们看到奥巴马试图行使这支笔的权力的最大领域。

sentences.en: And what he did was...
sentences.zh: 而他所做的是……

sentences.en: Right now, our power plants are the source of about a third of America's carbon pollution.
sentences.zh: 目前，我们的发电厂约占美国碳污染的三分之一。

sentences.en: He went to the EPA...
sentences.zh: 他找到了环保局……

sentences.en: But there have never been federal limits on the amount of carbon that power plants can dump into the air.
sentences.zh: 但联邦政府从未对发电厂排入空气中的碳排放量设定过限制。

sentences.en: Think about that.
sentences.zh: 想想看。

sentences.en: And he directed them to do this massive, sweeping, very unusual regulation.
sentences.zh: 他指示他们制定这项大规模、全面且非常不同寻常的法规。

sentences.en: And today we're here to announce America's Clean Power Plan.
sentences.zh: 今天我们来到这里，是为了宣布美国的“清洁电力计划”。

sentences.en: That was effectively designed to shut down these coal and gas-fired power plants.
sentences.zh: 该计划旨在关闭这些燃煤和燃气发电厂。

sentences.en: A plan two years in the making and the single most important step America has ever taken in the fight against global climate change.
sentences.zh: 这是一个历时两年制定的计划，也是美国在对抗全球气候变化斗争中所采取的最重要的单一举措。

sentences.en: And kind of totally transform the electricity sector of the U.S., sort of how we turn on the lights in America.
sentences.zh: 并且彻底重塑了美国的电力行业，改变了我们点亮美国的方式。

sentences.en: So, Coral, he couldn't do this through Congress, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，科拉，他无法通过国会做到这一点，对吧？

sentences.en: He tried and he failed.
sentences.zh: 他尝试过了，但失败了。

sentences.en: So he did it himself.
sentences.zh: 所以他自己动手了。

sentences.en: And I think people are largely familiar with this idea of executive action.
sentences.zh: 我想人们对行政行动这个概念大体上都很熟悉。

sentences.en: You know, Obama was famous for them, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，奥巴马以这著称，对吧？

sentences.en: But what exactly was this executive action based on legally?
sentences.zh: 但从法律上讲，这一行政行动究竟是基于什么？

sentences.en: I mean, how did he have that authority?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他怎么会有这种权力？

sentences.en: So, in order to do this, Obama relied on a very old and powerful tool, the 1970 Clean Air Act.
sentences.zh: 为了做到这一点，奥巴马借助了一个历史悠久且威力强大的工具，即1970年的《清洁空气法》。

sentences.en: Clean Air Act is known as the most powerful environmental law in the world.
sentences.zh: 《清洁空气法》被誉为世界上最强大的环境法。

sentences.en: Each of us all across this great land has a stake in maintaining and improving environmental quality.
sentences.zh: 这片伟大土地上的每一个人，都与维护和改善环境质量息息相关。

sentences.en: It was signed into law in 1970 by Richard Nixon.
sentences.zh: 它于1970年由理查德·尼克松签署成为法律。

sentences.en: The time has come for man to make his peace with nature.
sentences.zh: 人类与自然实现和平的时刻已经到来。

sentences.en: And it was designed to fundamentally give this brand new agency, the Environmental Protection Agency, a lot of authority to clean up the nation's air and water.
sentences.zh: 它旨在从根本上赋予这个全新的机构——环境保护局——巨大的权力，以净化国家的空气和水。

sentences.en: These problems will not stand still for politics or for partisanship.
sentences.zh: 这些问题不会因为政治或党派偏见而停滞不前。

sentences.en: They demand to be met now.
sentences.zh: 它们亟待我们现在去解决。

sentences.en: One of the things that makes the Clean Air Act very, very powerful is that its authors understood in the 1970s,
sentences.zh: 《清洁空气法》之所以非常非常强大，原因之一在于它的起草者在20世纪70年代就认识到，

sentences.en: there's probably going to be a lot of environmental problems of the future.
sentences.zh: 未来可能会出现许多环境问题。

sentences.en: Pollutants that are out there that we don't even know about.
sentences.zh: 还有一些我们甚至还不知道的污染物存在于世。

sentences.en: And we want to make sure that this agency, that the executive branch, can go after this stuff that we don't even know about.
sentences.zh: 我们希望确保这个机构、行政分支能够去应对这些我们甚至还不知道的东西。

sentences.en: So we want to make this broad and we want to give them a lot of authority.
sentences.zh: 所以我们希望让它涵盖范围广泛，并赋予他们很大的权力。

sentences.en: So it doesn't say,
sentences.zh: 因此，它并没有说，

sentences.en: hey, EPA, you explicitly have the authority to, you know, regulate carbon dioxide pollution from coal-fired power plants to deal with global warming.
sentences.zh: 嘿，环保局，你明确有权监管燃煤发电厂的二氧化碳污染，以应对全球变暖。

sentences.en: You know, they didn't really know that that was an issue then.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们当时并不知道那是一个问题。

sentences.en: They were imagining a future that had not yet happened.
sentences.zh: 他们在设想一个尚未发生的未来。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And so there are a lot of pieces in the Clean Air Act that are not specific, that are sort of broad and vague and that haven't really been used before.
sentences.zh: 因此，《清洁空气法》中有很多条款并不具体，它们有些宽泛且模糊，而且以前从未真正使用过。

sentences.en: And so when Obama, you know, realized, okay, I can't do a new climate change law, they sat down and they said, all right, we've got this thing.
sentences.zh: 所以当奥巴马意识到，好吧，我无法通过一项新的气候变化法律时，他们坐在一起说，好吧，我们有这个东西。

sentences.en: There's a section in the law, 111D of the Clean Air Act, never been used before.
sentences.zh: 法律中有一个条款，即《清洁空气法》第 111 条 D 款，以前从未被使用过。

sentences.en: You know, it's just been sitting there quietly in the statute for 50 years.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它已经在法案中静静地躺了50年。

sentences.en: And it's not exactly clear, but we could use it to do this.
sentences.zh: 虽然它不是特别清晰，但我们可以用它来做这件事。

sentences.en: I see.
sentences.zh: 我明白了。

sentences.en: And they knew at the time that that was very bold.
sentences.zh: 而且他们当时就知道这非常大胆。

sentences.en: The Obama administration knew.
sentences.zh: 奥巴马政府是知道这一点的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: They said, okay, we've got this imperfect old tool and let's go for it and give it a shot.
sentences.zh: 他们说，好吧，我们有这个不完美的旧工具，那就放手一搏吧。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So Obama based this executive action on a law that was old, that said nothing about carbon emissions or global warming.
sentences.zh: 所以奥巴马这一行政行动的基础是一部老旧的法律，里面根本没有提及碳排放或全球变暖。

sentences.en: So what happens after he does that?
sentences.zh: 那么在他这样做之后发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, within 24 hours, he's smacked with a giant lawsuit by all of these Republican attorneys general.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不到24小时，他就被所有这些共和党总检察长提起了一场巨大的诉讼。

sentences.en: The leader is the attorney general of one of the major coal producing states in the country, West Virginia.
sentences.zh: 领头的是国内主要产煤大国之一西弗吉尼亚州的总检察长。

sentences.en: He's flanked by some of the most powerful attorneys general from other states across the country.
sentences.zh: 他的身边是一些来自全国其他州的最具权力的总检察长。

sentences.en: And they say, oh, heck no.
sentences.zh: 他们说，门都没有。

sentences.en: You have stretched the intent of this law so far beyond, you know, how it was ever meant to be used.
sentences.zh: 你们对这部法律意图的曲解，远远超出了它原本的用途。

sentences.en: You've given this agency the authority to remake our entire electricity sector.
sentences.zh: 你们赋予了这个机构重塑我们整个电力行业的权力。

sentences.en: You have gone way, way too far in this.
sentences.zh: 你们在这件事上走得太远太远了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So he slapped with this lawsuit.
sentences.zh: 所以他吃了一场官司。

sentences.en: What happens to it?
sentences.zh: 这个案子后来怎么样了？

sentences.en: What do the courts do?
sentences.zh: 法院是怎么做的？

sentences.en: So the lawsuit starts moving in 2014.
sentences.zh: 所以诉讼在2014年开始推进。

sentences.en: And by 2016, there's a new president in town.
sentences.zh: 到了2016年，白宫迎来了新总统。

sentences.en: And this was a top priority for President Trump.
sentences.zh: 这对特朗普总统来说是重中之重。

sentences.en: So he effectively rolled back this regulation.
sentences.zh: 因此他实际上撤回了这项法规。

sentences.en: No more clean power plan.
sentences.zh: 清洁电力计划不复存在了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So the lawsuit is moot at that point then.
sentences.zh: 那么到那个时候，这起诉讼就没有实际意义了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: At that point, there's nothing to fight over until President Biden campaigns and comes into office on an even more passionate and aggressive climate change platform than Obama.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，在拜登总统开展竞选并带着比奥巴马更充满激情、更激进的气候变化纲领上台之前，没有什么可争论的了。

sentences.en: In his inauguration speech, he said that tackling climate change would be one of the four driving principles of his administration.
sentences.zh: 他在就职演说中表示，应对气候变化将是他政府的四大驱动原则之一。

sentences.en: You know, he said he wanted to do legislation, but he also wanted to reimpose these Obama-era climate change rules, but go further.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他说他想要通过立法，但也希望重新实施奥巴马时期的气候变化规则，甚至走得更远。

sentences.en: And so he made that intent very clear.
sentences.zh: 因此他非常明确地表达了这种意图。

sentences.en: However, it's only a year in, and they have not yet actually put any of that regulation back in place.
sentences.zh: 然而，一年过去了，他们实际上还没有把任何这些法规重新恢复到位。

sentences.en: While they have talked about it and been clear that at the EPA, they are working on formulating such a plan, there's not yet one on the books,
sentences.zh: 尽管他们已经讨论过这一点，并明确表示环保局正在致力于制定这样的计划，但目前还没有正式出台任何法规，

sentences.en: but the AGs, the Republican AGs, are continuing with this lawsuit.
sentences.zh: 不过总检察长们，也就是共和党总检察长们，仍在继续这场诉讼。

sentences.en: West Virginia versus EPA is continuing to make its way through the courts.
sentences.zh: 西弗吉尼亚州诉环保局案继续在各级法院审理。

sentences.en: And what is super weird about this case, and I've had sort of like the highest legal experts in the land use that extremely technical term in describing it, is that at this moment,
sentences.zh: 关于这个案件最诡异的地方在于——我曾听到全国顶级的法律专家用这个极其专业的术语来描述它——那就是在此刻，

sentences.en: it's a case about a regulation that doesn't exiSt.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于根本不存在的法规的案件。

sentences.en: Okay, that is very weird.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这真的很诡异。

sentences.en: It's, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But Coral, how does that actually work?
sentences.zh: 但是科拉，这到底是怎么运作的呢？

sentences.en: I mean, there's no regulation in place to fight, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，没有现行的法规可以对抗，对吧？

sentences.en: So how are the courts able to just pick it up if there's no other side?
sentences.zh: 那么如果没有另一方，法院怎么能直接审理呢？

sentences.en: That is a great question, Sabrina.
sentences.zh: 这是个好问题，萨布丽娜。

sentences.en: It is a question that I don't think we fully have an answer yet to, because it's so unusual and new, and it's this very aggressive legal strategy
sentences.zh: 我认为我们还没有完全找到答案，因为它太不寻常、太新颖了，这是一种非常激进的法律策略，

sentences.en: that's about shutting down these regulations preemptively.
sentences.zh: 旨在先发制人地叫停这些法规。

sentences.en: Okay, so this is a lawsuit being effectively reanimated by people opposed to the government regulating carbon emissions who are so intent on blocking that regulation
sentences.zh: 好的，所以这是一场由反对政府监管碳排放的人重新激活的诉讼，他们决心阻止该法规，

sentences.en: that they're preemptively suing to stop something that doesn't even exist yet and taking that theoretical case all the way up to the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 以至于他们先发制人地起诉以阻止甚至尚不存在的东西，并将这个理论上的案件一直上诉到最高法院。

sentences.en: Yes, and so this case is going to be one of the first times we'll see
sentences.zh: 是的，所以这个案件将是我们首次看到

sentences.en: a major case like this be decided.
sentences.zh: 这样一个重大案件得到裁决。

sentences.en: We haven't really seen the Supreme Court make a decision like this.
sentences.zh: 我们以前没怎么见过最高法院做出这样的决定。

sentences.en: And that is why this is such an important and interesting case with so much impact.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么这是一个如此重要、有趣且影响深远的案件。

sentences.en: And so we'll see.
sentences.zh: 所以我们拭目以待。

sentences.en: We'll come out on the other side of that in the next few days, maybe in the next week.
sentences.zh: 我们在接下来的几天里，也许是一周内，就会看到结果。

sentences.en: But, you know, something that's very important to know is there will be profound impacts not just for how and whether the EPA can regulate climate warming pollution
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，有一点非常重要，那就是它将产生深远的影响，不仅关乎环保局如何以及能否监管气候变暖污染，

sentences.en: or even how and whether the EPA can do environmental rules.
sentences.zh: 甚至关乎环保局如何以及能否制定环境规则。

sentences.en: This is likely to have a big impact on how the entire federal government can make rules and regulate.
sentences.zh: 这很可能会对整个联邦政府如何制定规则和监管产生重大影响。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·荣森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design, and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《变革者》，这是一个专注于设计之美以及围绕它的文化的播客。

sentences.en: Coral, how might this case, this West Virginia versus EPA,

sentences.en: This is part of a very long, very carefully coordinated, very well-funded campaign on the right to go after something much bigger, not just this one particular regulation,

sentences.zh: 而是要去针对许多保守派激进人士所称的行政国家。

sentences.en: What is the administrative state?
sentences.zh: 什么是行政国家？

sentences.en: It's kind of a buzzword that a lot of conservatives and conservative activists and conservative legal scholars and conservative attorneys have talked about
sentences.zh: 这算是一个流行语，许多保守派、保守派激进人士、保守派法律学者和保守派律师都在讨论它，

sentences.en: as this kind of bloated executive branch, this idea that there's, you know, thousands and thousands of unelected bureaucrats sitting in federal agencies

sentences.en: making regulation after rule that have so much effect on our lives and on the economy.

sentences.en: And that is the broader target of a lot of these cases is to create a new legal precedent that will rein that all in and prune it down.
sentences.zh: 而这正是其中许多案件的更广泛目标，即创造一个新的法律先例，将这一切全盘收紧并大大削减。

sentences.en: So, okay, the administrative state and the conservative argument against it, I get that.
sentences.zh: 好吧，行政国家以及保守派反对它的论点，我明白了。

sentences.en: But how are they going after this administrative state?

sentences.en: I mean, what are they actually doing?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们实际在做什么？

sentences.en: So there is a really specific legal doctrine that has been in place since the 1980s that conservatives see in many ways as giving rise to the executive branch having so much power.
sentences.zh: 自20世纪80年代以来，一直存在一项非常具体的法律原则，在保守派看来，正是这项原则在许多方面赋予了行政部门如此巨大的权力。

sentences.en: This legal doctrine stems from a Supreme Court decision called Chevron versus NRDC and it led to what is known as
sentences.zh: 这项法律原则源于最高法院的一个判例，名为雪佛龙诉自然资源保护委员会案（Chevron versus NRDC），它引出了所谓的

sentences.en: Chevron deference.

sentences.en: So what does that mean?
sentences.zh: 那这是什么意思？

sentences.en: Yes, what does that mean?

sentences.en: What does that mean?
sentences.zh: 那到底是什么意思？

sentences.en: So in that case, it found that when a law is not clear or not specific on how to do rules and regulations, then the federal agencies get deference.

sentences.en: They get to interpret it.

sentences.en: They get the authority.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有这种权威。

sentences.en: So, you know, in the case of this Clean Power Plan that we've been talking about, the Obama administration kind of leaned on the existence of this Chevron deference and said,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，在我们一直在讨论的这个《清洁电力计划》案中，奥巴马政府有点倚重雪佛龙司法尊让原则的存在，并表示，

sentences.en: okay, you have this old
sentences.zh: 好吧，你们有这个古老的

sentences.en: 1970 Clean Air Act doesn't talk about any of these things, but this Chevron deference means the EPA has deference.

sentences.en: They can take the broad outlines of what's there and they can fill it in.

sentences.en: They can use their, you know, science and expertise and economic expertise and they can make a whole new regulation.
sentences.zh: 他们可以利用，你知道的，他们的科学专业知识、经济专业知识，从而制定出一整套全新的法规。

sentences.en: They have the deference.
sentences.zh: 他们享有这种尊让权。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有意思。

sentences.en: So the name would suggest that the deference is to Chevron, but you're saying that the deference actually goes to federal agencies.
sentences.zh: 所以这个名字暗示着这种尊让是给雪佛龙的，但你的意思是这种尊让实际上是给联邦机构的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.zh: 但在这里拥有尊让权到底意味着什么？

sentences.en: So this is, this is something that's used kind of across the federal government, but especially really, you know, in the EPA, there are examples of laws on clean air,
sentences.zh: 所以这是，这是整个联邦政府都在使用的一种机制，但尤其是，你知道的，在环保署，有很多关于清洁空气的法律实例，

sentences.en: laws on clean water, where, you know, you see the broad strokes sort of laying out, well, you know, we want you to regulate this pollutant, we want you to take care
sentences.zh: 关于清洁水的法律，在这里，你知道的，你会看到大体上的轮廓勾勒出，好吧，你知道的，我们希望你监管这种污染物，我们希望你处理

sentences.en: And so through the decades, you know, the EPA has used the Clean Air Act to do all kinds of very powerful regulations on things like

sentences.en: If you have, you know, laws about financial regulation that aren't specific on what the regulators should do, like the SEC, the people over in that building get to figure it out

sentences.en: That is sort of
sentences.zh: 这就是那种

sentences.en: Chevron deference at work.

sentences.en: I mean, the broad goal of this is to shut down this one particular regulation but use this as a wrecking ball to kind of take a first thwack at this idea of the Chevron deference.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这一切的广泛目标是叫停这一项特定的法规，但以此作为一颗重锤，对雪佛龙尊让这个概念进行第一波强力打击。

sentences.en: OK, but the top line of that argument that power should go back into the hands of elected officials,

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，

sentences.en: No.

sentences.en: Maybe this is the point for the Republican AGs behind this case, right?

sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，那些共和党总检察长们，

sentences.en: There are others who are not going to go that far, but who will say any kind of regulation on fossil fuel devastates my home state's economy, so my objective is no regulation

sentences.en: for that reason.

sentences.zh: 然后，你知道的，我认为这个集团的领导者们在最高法院前发表公开辩论时，将其拔高到了一个更高的层面，即，

sentences.en: I think that there is a very good shot because, you know, it's not new.

sentences.en: All of the pieces of this strategy have been slowly being put in place for,

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，真正要追溯到奥巴马政府时期，而且在特朗普政府时期更是如此，由特朗普政府挑选进入最高法院的法官们，不仅是在最高法院，一直延伸到整个联邦司法系统的各个层级，在许多情况下，他们都想要那些有着某种反对行政状态、反对雪佛龙尊让记录的法官。

sentences.en: by the Trump administration, not just on the Supreme Court, but all the way down through the federal judiciary, in many cases, they wanted judges who had some kind of record

sentences.en: of being opposed to the administrative state, being opposed to Chevron deference.

sentences.zh: 尼尔·戈萨奇（Neil Gorsuch），当然，他将对这个案件做出裁决，他曾在一份著名的异议中写道，雪佛龙尊让允许行政官僚机构吞噬了大量的
